why: Both show correct 63/47/24% values, but B uses a subtitle that states an actual finding (2.6x) and a tighter layout, while A's corner footnote just repeats the top bar's label.

A sorts the ordinal cylinder counts by value (8,6,3,5,4), uses a rocket palette that leaves the key 158 hp bar a near-invisible pale cream, and lets its label collide with the title; B keeps the natural 3-8 order in one uniform colour.
The charts are nearly identical, but A labels the 2024 record bar directly, while B's title (1880-2024) disagrees with its corner note (1880 to 2025).

B orders species by mass, makes the medians visible with red markers and labels them with units, and adds a subtitle on Gentoo's lead; A's medians are faint grey ticks and its top label crowds the title.

A colours the average dots on a red-to-pale-yellow scale, so the weaker models' averages nearly vanish on white and the legend's yellow 'Average' swatch doesn't match the red dots; B keeps one consistent colour per role and states the finding in the subtitle.

Same heatmap, but B's subtitle states the point the task cares about (mpg vs weight, r=-0.83) and its colorbar matches the dimgrey styling, while A's footnote highlights displacement vs weight instead.

A is rainbow spaghetti where colour means nothing; B puts the individual chicks in grey under a bold mean line, labels each diet's endpoint and states the comparison across diets in a subtitle, with a shared y-axis.
A produced no chart; B delivers both PR and ROC panels with fold curves, an average curve and a no-skill baseline.

A uses a sequential blue-grey palette on a linear GDP axis, so continents can't be told apart and the relationship is squashed against the left edge; B uses a log x-axis with distinct colours and markers per continent.
A labels each line at its end in distinct hues, while B uses five near-identical shades of blue with a separate legend, so the lines can't be matched to their symbols.
A marks the median (the right summary for a skewed distribution) with a clean label and light styling; B's mean label box sits on top of the peak bar and the full grid and frame add clutter.

A's italic annotation overlaps the 96.8% bar label and it prints a stray '0.0%' label at the base of the 1st-class pair; B is clean and correct (97%/14%), with only a minor 96% vs 97% wording slip in the subtitle.
